title: Cache-Line Contention and Stack-Frame Layout in a PHP Bytecode Virtual Machine with Balanced Indexing
topic: Bytecode Virtual Machine with Stack Evaluation Engine

abstract: A lightweight stack-based bytecode virtual machine (VM) written in PHP is examined for its interaction with modern server-class hardware. The VM implements a balanced search tree to index bytecode offsets, enabling constant-time stack manipulation while preserving logarithmic lookup for jump targets. Formal invariants guarantee stack height balance and key-ordered indexing, which are proved in Section 4. Empirical evaluation on an AMD EPYC 7763 (1 core / 2 threads, 7.8~GB RAM, Linux 6.17) shows a mean latency of 40 501.52 \textmu{}s ($\sigma$ = 606.14 \textmu{}s) and a throughput of 24 690 ops/s over 30 runs. These results illustrate the impact of cache-line contention on a high-level language VM and provide a reproducible baseline for future optimizations. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/php-backend-core/tree/main/algorithms/20261010_150519\_bytecode\_virtual\_machine\_with}.
author: Mateus Yonathan
